sources.author: Swyx (Shawn Wang)
sources.headline: Founder @ Latent Space | AI Engineer
sources.post_summary: Claude's new token-efficient tool use dropped yesterday and nobody's talking about how it changes the cost math for agentic loops. I ran a benchmark: 3x fewer tokens on multi-step tool calls. If you're billing by input tokens, your agent costs just got restructured overnight.

sources.author: Lenny Rachitsky
sources.headline: Author of Lenny's Newsletter | Product & Growth
sources.post_summary: I interviewed 40 PMs who've shipped AI features in the last 6 months. The ones who flopped shared one pattern: they let the model decide UX. The ones who won kept the model in the engine room and put humans at the wheel. AI autonomy is a dial, not a switch.

sources.author: Alessio Fanelli
sources.headline: Partner @ Decibel Ventures | Co-host Latent Space Podcast
sources.post_summary: The new wave of AI infra companies isn't competing on model quality anymore — it's competing on orchestration latency and observability. We just led a seed into a team building structured trace tooling for multi-agent systems. Debugging agents is the new DevOps.

sources.author: Aman Khan
sources.headline: Staff Eng @ [stealth] | prev Stripe | building in AI infra
sources.post_summary: Hot take: most 'AI automation' demos you see on LinkedIn are scripted. Real production agents fail 30-40% of the time on edge cases nobody thought to test. The companies winning right now aren't the ones with the best models — they're the ones with the best evals and the tightest fallback loops.

sources.author: Kyle Poyar
sources.headline: Operating Partner at OpenView | Growth & PLG Advisor
sources.post_summary: Most outbound teams are optimizing the wrong thing. They're measuring email open rates while their best-fit accounts are making buying decisions in Slack communities and Reddit threads they'll never see. The shift from channel-based outbound to signal-based outbound is real — companies doing it right are booking 3x more meetings with half the headcount. Here's what the modern stack actually looks like.

sources.author: Liam Moroney
sources.headline: Head of Marketing @ Teal | B2B Demand Gen & Revenue Ops
sources.post_summary: Unpopular opinion: most 'GTM engineers' are just RevOps people who learned to use Clay. Real GTM engineering means owning the system end-to-end — from ICP signal ingestion through enrichment, scoring, routing, and sequence personalization — with code, not just no-code workflows. The bar is rising fast and most teams are 12 months behind where they need to be.

sources.author: Gaetano DiNardi
sources.headline: Growth Advisor | Former VP Marketing @ Cognism, Nextiva, Sales Hacker
sources.post_summary: Content strategy in 2026 looks nothing like 2023. Dark social is the dominant distribution channel — your buyers are sharing your content in DMs, Slack groups, and WhatsApp threads you can't attribute. If your entire content budget is chasing tracked clicks and UTM parameters, you're optimizing a system that's already dead. The founders winning are publishing consistently on LinkedIn and letting word-of-mouth compound.

sources.author: Jen Allen-Knuth
sources.headline: Community Growth @ Lavender | Challenger Sale Practitioner | Ex-Challenger Inc.
sources.post_summary: I reviewed 200 cold emails sent by AI agents last month. 94% of them opened with a compliment about the company's 'impressive growth' or referenced a LinkedIn post from 6 months ago. Buyers are already pattern-matching AI outreach and deleting it instantly. The reps winning aren't sending smarter AI emails — they're sending fewer, more specific ones that show they actually read the prospect's last earnings call or product launch.

sources.author: Priya Nair
sources.headline: Solo founder | Built and sold my first SaaS in 14 months | Now building #2
sources.post_summary: Priya shares a raw breakdown of her first $10k MRR month — including the three features she almost built that would have killed the product. She leads with the specific Stripe screenshot and walks through the decision to ignore enterprise requests and stay focused on the indie hacker segment.

sources.author: Marcus Webb
sources.headline: ex-Finance → Software Engineer | 18 months of self-teaching | Now at Stripe
sources.post_summary: Marcus posts a before/after of his life two years apart — Excel spreadsheets vs. a pull request merged into Stripe's codebase. He breaks down the exact curriculum he followed, which resources he wasted money on, and what finally clicked. Ends with a call to DM him if you're considering the same pivot.

sources.author: Lena Hoffman
sources.headline: Building Clio — AI research assistant for solo consultants | Day 1 in public
sources.post_summary: Lena announces she's shipping a full SaaS in 30 days using Claude's API and Next.js, with daily updates posted publicly. She shares her Notion roadmap, her first 47 waitlist signups from a single tweet, and the moment she almost gave up on day 3. Closes with her week-one revenue: $340.

sources.author: Dev Patel
sources.headline: Founder @ Stackform | Vibe-coded my way to $50k ARR | Claude Code addict
sources.post_summary: Dev argues that the skill gap between a great engineer and a great founder has never been smaller — he built his entire backend using Claude Code without writing a single line of SQL from scratch. He breaks down exactly which parts AI got wrong, where he had to intervene, and why the bottleneck is now distribution, not engineering.
